summary.headline: Dabur Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 10.6%, with India FMCG up 9.5% on 5% volume growth and international up 15.5% in INR.
summary.overview: Consolidated business grew 10.6% in Q1 FY27 with India FMCG at 9.5% (5% volume) and international at 15.5% in INR terms. HPC grew 12.3% led by hair care, where hair oil grew about 18% (roughly half volume, half price). Operating margin rose 11% and PAT rose 15%, both ahead of revenue. Management guided to sequential acceleration in revenue growth and double-digit consolidated revenue growth for the full year, while flagging that volumes will be under pressure from inflation and Middle East war-linked crude costs.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / net cash position (as stated)
financial_highlights.value: approximately INR9,000 crore net debt; INR9,500 crore liquid cash and investments cited by analyst

segments.name: Hair care (hair oil and shampoo)
segments.commentary: Hair oil grew about 18% (around 8% volume, balance price) and shampoo grew strong double digits; market share gained 107 bps in hair oil. Management said Hindi belt is a number 2 hair oil penetrated brand.

segments.name: Oral care
segments.commentary: Near double-digit growth led by Red, Meswak and Dabur Herbal; Lal Dant Manjan grew double digit. Herbal segment outperformed non-herbal by 550 bps.

segments.name: Skin care
segments.commentary: High single-digit growth driven by Gulabari and OxyLife.

segments.name: Home care
segments.commentary: Mid-single-digit growth; Odonil high single digit with about 80 bps share gain; Sanifresh grew high teens.

segments.name: Health care
segments.commentary: Health supplements low single digit; honey high single digit with 150 bps share gain; Honitus up 25%; Pudin Hara double digit; health juices mid-20s; Siens grew 3x. Glucose hit by April rains, recovered in May-June at mid-teens.

segments.name: Foods (Badshah)
segments.commentary: Foods grew around 30%; Badshah grew 13.3% with about 11% domestic volume growth and no price increase. E-commerce and quick commerce are about 6% of Badshah turnover.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Beverage portfolio grew mid-teens in May-June after April disruption; active juices grew over 40% and coconut water over 70%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Grew 15.5% in INR: MENA about 9%, UK and EU 22%, Egypt 28%, Turkey 27%, Bangladesh 34%. Benefited from currency tailwind.

guidance_outlook: Management expects sequential acceleration in revenue growth in coming quarters.
Double-digit consolidated revenue growth targeted for full FY27, with hair oil also guided to double-digit growth.
Margins expected to be better than last year and accretive to top-line growth for the full year, contingent on the Middle East war and crude-linked inflation.
Volumes expected to be under pressure from inflation; growth to be driven more by price and value than volume.
Acquisition target: 1 or 2 sizable companies over about 3 years; INR500 crore earmarked for Dabur Ventures (D2C).
Greenfield capex in Tamil Nadu expected to consume roughly INR400-500 crore of cash.
capex_capacity: Greenfield project in Tamil Nadu planned; around INR400-500 crore cash outflow globally cited for routine expansion.
INR500 crore allocated for D2C acquisitions via Dabur Ventures; minority stake first, then move to majority once profitable.
Siens nutraceutical brand expected to exit FY27 at roughly INR50 crore ARR.
Badshah exit run-rate around INR400 crore, up from about INR220 crore at acquisition.
demand_pricing: Rural growing ahead of urban: Dabur rural growth about 550 bps above urban (GT only); Nielsen rural ahead by 170 bps.
Hair oil growth about 50% volume and 50% price; price increases taken due to crude-linked LLP cost increases and GST-driven pricing.
Monsoon deficit reported at 14-15% after recent rains, seen as supportive for Kharif.
Spices deflationary for Badshah; growth entirely volume-led.
Odonil grew despite raw material shortages; glucose and juices were hit by April unseasonal rains and seasonality.
Competition in D2C and food categories noted by analyst; Badshah present in Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan and Delhi NCR.

qa_highlights.question: How has Badshah expanded beyond its two original states, and is double-digit volume growth enough?
qa_highlights.answer: Badshah grew 13.3% with about 11% domestic volume growth; it has expanded into MP, Rajasthan and Delhi NCR. E-commerce and quick commerce are about 6% of turnover and growing at triple digits; exit run-rate is about INR400 crore versus INR220 crore at acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Did Glucose and fruit juice recover in May-June, and is there a structural issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April was the disruption; May-June saw mid-teens growth in glucose and high-teens in juices. Glucose is rural and seasonal; 100% juices grew about 45%, coconut water about 70%, and Nectar turned profitable in the second half of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the D2C acquisition timeline and what disruptive innovations are working?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 1 or 2 sizable acquisitions in about 3 years, with talks ongoing with 2 or 3 companies; execution depends on negotiation. Siens is the disruptive innovation, expected to exit FY27 at about INR50 crore ARR.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hair oil volume growth and outlook, and is full-year double-digit growth intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Hair oil grew about 18%, with 8% volume. Management is confident of double-digit hair oil growth next quarter and maintained double-digit consolidated revenue growth for the full year, with currency as a tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: What is the monsoon and rural outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the monsoon deficit has narrowed to about 14-15% after recent rains and rural is resilient, with Dabur rural about 550 bps ahead of urban; inflation is a concern but government MSP support is positive.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance be deployed, and can PAT growth of 14-15% be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR9,000 crore, of which about INR6,500 crore is in India. Priorities: acquisitions, dividends (100% of India profits paid out), and capex. Management said volumes will not be double-digit and profit growth depends on whether the war and crude-linked inflation ease.

risks_watch: Middle East war driving crude-linked raw material and packaging inflation, which could hit margins and volume.
Volume pressure as price increases are passed on; management says volume growth will not be double-digit.
Glucose and juice seasonality and competition from energy drinks and cola brands.
Execution of Saksham go-to-market transformation and the pace of the D2C acquisition pipeline.
Currency tailwind from international business may not persist; sequential revenue acceleration to be confirmed next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and profit momentum, with growth figures cited for most categories. Cautious on the outlook, saying growth depends on the Middle East war and crude-linked inflation. Evasive on the acquisition timeline and the capital allocation question, deferring to negotiations and the board.
key_quotes: Against this backdrop, Dabur delivered a strong start to the year.
Volumes will be under pressure as the inflation is too much.
It all depends upon the war. If the war ends tomorrow, then I think the petroleum prices will come down, and therefore crude-linked inflation will come down.

adds.what: Greenfield project in Tamil Nadu (capacity size not stated)

growth.why: Management maintains double-digit FY27 consolidated revenue growth and expects sequential acceleration, backed by price-led hair oil growth, share gains and international (+15.5% INR), but flags volume pressure from inflation; capacity support is limited to an unsized Tamil Nadu greenfield (~INR400-500 crore).
